title: Normative Requirement Validation Correspondence Contract
purpose: Defines the canonical repository-generic semantic contract relating active normative requirements to validation-correspondence packages, validation tasks, source-local validation-callable roles, lifecycle state, and subordinate validation evidence.

normative_requirements.text: The repository shall define `repo.validation-correspondence` as the single controlling repository-generic normative owner for normative-requirement validation-correspondence semantics. Validation correspondence shall remain subordinate to the normative requirement whose conformance it records or enforces and shall not restate, amend, infer, or replace that requirement's semantics.

A canonical normative reference used by validation correspondence shall be a structured object containing exactly `spec_id` and `requirement_id`, where `spec_id` identifies the owning accepted specification and `requirement_id` identifies one stable active or historical normative requirement within that specification. Bare requirement identifiers shall not be treated as repository-global join keys. For an active canonical package, the package source path shall be deterministically derived from normative ownership and that canonical reference as `<validation-domain>/validation/packages/<spec_id>/<requirement_id>.json`, where `<validation-domain>` is the owning root selected by `repo.repository-structure`: repository-owned requirements use `repo`, product-owned requirements use `product`, and the checkout root is used only when accepted authority explicitly assigns canonical package ownership to an inherently cross-domain or whole-checkout normative responsibility. The path shall not be independently registered in a second requirement-to-package mapping.

Every active normative requirement owned by an accepted repository specification registered by `repo.manifest`, and every active normative requirement owned by an accepted governed product specification registered by `repo.product-manifest`, shall have exactly one active validation-correspondence package relationship. Candidate or other non-normative specification state may prepare non-active correspondence without satisfying or changing active completeness. Withdrawn or historical requirements shall not retain active package ownership.

Each active validation-correspondence package relationship shall be represented by one maintained JSON source object whose canonical package identity is its canonical normative reference. The object shall contain exactly one canonical normative reference, one `validation_disposition`, optional `validation_rationale` subject to the disposition rules, and a `tasks` collection containing zero or more externally identified validation-task records. The exhaustive validation-disposition vocabulary shall be `mechanical`, `partial`, `semantic-review`, and `not-applicable`. `mechanical` means repository mechanical validation is expected to establish the requirement's objectively enforceable conformance; `partial` means mechanical validation establishes objective portions but complete conformance also requires semantic review; `semantic-review` means meaningful conformance is primarily review-owned rather than mechanically provable; and `not-applicable` means repository-local executable validation does not apply to the governed behavior. `partial`, `semantic-review`, and `not-applicable` shall require a non-empty rationale; `mechanical` shall not require one. Package completeness and validation-task population remain distinct, and zero tasks shall not by itself make a package incomplete.

Each externally identified validation task shall have a stable `task_id` that is unique across the active repository validation-correspondence package set and shall never be reused for unrelated validation behavior after publication. A task record shall resolve to one repository-relative maintained source path and one callable identifier, shall belong through exactly one package to exactly one canonical normative reference, and may additionally carry purpose/coverage-intent and execution-level metadata. Source path and callable identifier are mutable implementation coordinates and may change without changing task identity when the maintained validation responsibility is materially the same. Fixtures, parameter cases, assertions, and non-callable internals are not independently required to receive task identity. Shared internal helpers may support multiple tasks or normative requirements but shall not thereby acquire task or normative-requirement ownership.

Every maintained callable defined in governed validation implementation source shall be source-locally classifiable at an exact revision as exactly one mutually exclusive role: validation-task callable or helper. A validation-task callable shall expose machine-readable source-local metadata identifying its stable `task_id` and exactly one canonical normative reference; a helper shall expose its non-owning helper role and shall not simultaneously claim task or normative-requirement ownership. The repository shall use one canonical source-local metadata mechanism per maintained validation implementation language/domain, but the concrete language syntax remains implementation-selected. Package records remain the canonical correspondence source model, and source-local metadata is subordinate traceability metadata that must mechanically agree with package ownership. A validation-task callable remains distinct from a public validation entry point governed by `repo.validation`.

Canonical package correspondence and source-local validation-callable correspondence shall mechanically agree. The canonical package relationship is the correspondence source model; source-local role and normative-reference metadata are subordinate traceability metadata and shall not become a second independently maintained requirement-to-validation registry.

Validation-task purpose or coverage intent and validation-task execution level shall be separate classification dimensions. The accepted purpose/coverage-intent vocabulary shall be `positive`, `negative`, `boundary`, and `regression`; the accepted execution-level vocabulary shall be `unit` and `integration`. A task may carry zero or more purpose/coverage-intent values and zero or one execution-level value. These dimensions describe validation evidence and execution organization only; they shall not alter the task's canonical normative ownership.

Repository-defined validation-correspondence invariants shall apply uniformly to active product-owned normative requirements without transferring product semantic ownership into repository validation authority. Product correspondence may retain product implementation, test-artifact, and conformance records, but normative requirement association for product test-artifact mappings shall resolve through applicable canonical validation-correspondence package relationships rather than through an independently maintained requirement-to-test registry.

Validation-correspondence integrity shall preserve active-package uniqueness, stable validation-task identity, task source-location and callable resolution, task-to-package uniqueness, source/package agreement, non-active treatment of withdrawn requirements, and deterministic subordinate projections. Package lifecycle shall distinguish preparatory, active, and historical correspondence state. Candidate or other non-normative specification state may carry preparatory package material, but preparatory material shall not satisfy active completeness and shall not be treated as an active package. Acceptance of the owning normative requirement shall require exactly one corresponding active package relationship. When a requirement is withdrawn, merged, moved, superseded, or otherwise ceases to be active, its package shall cease active ownership in the same governed transition and may be retained only as historical provenance; any surviving active semantics shall be represented by the active package or packages of the surviving requirements. Generated or materialized correspondence views shall remain deterministic subordinate projections according to `repo.authority-model`; physical projection implementation and migration mechanics remain later governed work.

When canonical validation correspondence is copied, generated, projected, installed, initialized, or otherwise materialized into another maintained validation surface, the materialized form shall preserve the same canonical package identity and normative reference, package lifecycle state, validation disposition, and externally identified validation-task ownership represented by the authoritative correspondence source. Materialized or propagated surfaces shall remain subordinate to the canonical source according to `repo.authority-model` and shall not become separately mutable correspondence registries. Repository validation shall be able to detect stale, missing, duplicated, or semantically divergent propagated correspondence without the propagation mechanism acquiring independent normative authority. Migration from a pre-correspondence or partially populated repository state shall preserve valid accepted revisions: preparatory or other explicitly non-active correspondence may be staged where accepted lifecycle rules permit it, and an Atomic authority transition shall be used only when the existing `repo.development-workflow` Atomic eligibility contract proves that no valid intermediate accepted revision exists. Exact copy/generation mechanics, initializer inventory, freshness algorithm, migration batching, bootstrap tooling, and migration sequence remain implementation-plan or maintained-artifact concerns.
